top_categories.workout_context: 17,717ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 105, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at L'Etape du Tour de France. Practice on alpine mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 105 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Etape du Tour de France's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
168ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 105 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
At L'Etape du Tour de France, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
17,717ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Etape du Tour de France. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at L'Etape du Tour de France. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on alpine mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
105 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.heat: July in Bourg d'Oisans → Alpe d'Huez (via Col de Sarenne) can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before L'Etape du Tour de France. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for L'Etape du Tour de France’s 105 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: L'Etape du Tour de France reaches approximately 8,700ft above sea level. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at L'Etape du Tour de France demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride alpine mountain passes at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Durability, and Road Specific to prepare you for 105 miles of alpine mountain passes in Bourg d'Oisans → Alpe d'Huez (via Col de Sarenne).
